face: Very well, {player}. I shall accept your alliance, though I expect the council to hear of it before the week is out, and I will not be the one who explains why.
An alliance, then. How convenient. Lords who come asking for favours are often the first to forget them, so I shall keep a careful ledger.
I accept. Let us put the terms in writing so that no one, least of all {rival}, can later claim we agreed to something we did not.
Agreed. Mark that I was the one who extended the hand first, should the minutes ever be read aloud at the next assembly.
Fine. Your banners may fly beside mine for now, though I have seen many such arrangements dissolve once the harvest taxes fall due.
I shall accept, {player}. Do not mistake courtesy for trust. I simply prefer to keep my rivals where I can see them.
Very well. I will bring the proposal before the council tomorrow, where I am certain a few members will ask questions you may not enjoy answering.
Accepted. I am sure {rival} will be delighted to hear of it, or will at least pretend to be, which at court amounts to much the same thing.
Gladly, {player}! Together our fiefs could outvote everyone who has been sneering at us in the great hall, and I do enjoy the thought of that.
You have made a sensible choice, and I would hate for you to regret it. Let us draft the charter before someone else thinks of the idea.
I accept with real pleasure. Between the two of us, the council seats will fall to people who actually understand how this realm works.
Splendid. I had hoped you would come to me first, and I shall tell the others the idea was mine from the start, naturally.
Yes, yes, a thousand times yes. Bring your envoys to supper and we will sort out who gets which fief over a very good bottle of wine.
Agreed, and happily so. With you at my side, {rival} will find it much harder to explain away the failed grain levy in front of the assembly.
I accept, {player}. You have a sharp mind for these matters, and I suspect we will recruit a few more allies before the next vote.
A wise decision, and one I shall be sure to mention when the next council seat is discussed. Shall we say the bell tower at dusk?
